claims.text: USGS recorded a magnitude 7.4 earthquake on 10 August 2026 at 12:34:28 UTC, located 5 km S of San José del Palmar, Colombia (4.8436°N, -76.2422°W) at a depth of 110.3 km. USGS's PAGER system assessed an Orange alert level, with approximately 10.5 million people exposed to Strong-to-Very-Strong (MMI VI+) shaking.

OCHA's Addendum to the Humanitarian Response Plan -- Earthquake, Colombia (posted 20 August 2026, originally published 19 August 2026): "According to the most recent reports as of 17 August, 304 people had lost their lives and 4,400 had been injured... Damage to housing is extensive: 134,341 homes have been affected and 29,554 have been destroyed... 267 residential buildings collapsed... Search and rescue activities remain ongoing and have enabled the rescue of 338 people."

Re-checked 12 August 2026: GDACS's earthquake report for this event (event id 1557236, episode 1724218) has escalated to an Overall Red alert for high humanitarian impact, with a GDACS score of 2.2 (up from 1.7) and about 5.2 million people now within zones of MMI VII or greater shaking (up from about 1.5 million). The page's casualty line, citing media reports and not independently verified by GDACS, now reads 'at least 240 deaths' -- higher than, and not adopted in place of, the government-sourced UN News figure below.

UN News (11 August 2026), 'Colombia earthquake: UN joins national response': citing Colombia's president, 'more than 180 have died' and 'hundreds have been injured'; 'nearly 5,000 homes have been damaged and 387 have been destroyed'; '61 buildings have collapsed'; 'more than 550 educational institutions, 24 health facilities and more than 350 community centres have [been] affected'; the government has activated emergency coordination centres in Bogotá, Quibdó, Armenia and Cali and has requested UN support.

Servicio Geológico Colombiano (10 August 2026): confirms the magnitude 7.4 event centered near San José del Palmar at a depth of about 103 km, recorded 18 aftershocks (magnitude 1.4-4.8) as of midday 10 August, describes it as 'the seismic event of greatest magnitude recorded in Colombia in the 21st century,' and notes more than 12,000 people from 900 populated centres reported feeling the earthquake. The bulletin gives no casualty figures.

USGS's PAGER alert for the earthquake (event us6000tjl2) escalated to Red as of 13 August 2026 06:30:47 UTC (magnitude 7.4, MMI 7.999, CDI 7.9, 1,121 felt reports), up from the Orange level recorded 11 August 2026.

OCHA Colombia's Flash Update 004 (posted 13 August 2026, data as of 12 August 18:30 local time): 'The emergency continues to escalate and has exceeded the local response capacity, with at least 49,214 people affected, 30,324 families impacted, 3,771 injured people, and 241 fatalities across 13 departments of the country... Damage to more than 54,900 homes (destroyed and damaged)... the USD 5 million CERF allocation represents a critical boost to scale up the emergency response.'

OCHA Colombia, Flash Update 005 (as of 13 August, 18:30 local time): "The scale of the emergency continues to grow. Heavy rainfall and related impacts have affected 53,816 people (25,872 families) across at least 13 departments and 401 municipalities nationwide, including 266 deaths and 11,789 homes destroyed. The most affected departments are Risaralda, Valle del Cauca, Chocó and Caldas. However, the emergency continues to expand and figures may increase due to access constraints and possible underreporting."

OCHA Colombia's Flash Update No. 006 (data as of 14 August 2026, 18:30 local time): 287 deaths, 3,975 injured, 378 missing, 135,179 affected people (56,448 affected families) across 15 departments and 437 municipalities, 13,077 homes destroyed; 183 aftershocks have followed the mainshock (15 of magnitude >3, two >4); an initial US$5 million CERF allocation is supporting the response.

OCHA Colombia's Flash Update No. 007 (posted 18 August 2026, data as of 17 August 2026, 20:00 local time): "According to official data, at least 186,182 people (121,470 families), including ethnic communities (Afro-Colombian and Indigenous peoples), have been affected by the impacts, including fatalities, injuries, and missing persons, as well as the loss of or damage to housing." Key figures: 304 deaths reported, 4,400 injured, 426 missing, 26,558 homes destroyed, across 15 departments and 472 most-affected municipalities.

description: A magnitude 7.4 intermediate-depth earthquake struck western Colombia on 10 August 2026 at 12:34:28 UTC, centered 5 km south of San José del Palmar in Chocó Department at a depth of roughly 110 km; Colombia's geological survey described it as the seismic event of greatest magnitude recorded in the country in the 21st century. OCHA Colombia's Flash Update 007 and its Addendum to the Humanitarian Response Plan (data as of 17 August) put the toll at 304 deaths, 4,400 injured and 426 missing, with 186,182 people (121,470 families) affected across 15 departments and 472 municipalities; 29,554 homes have been destroyed and search-and-rescue operations have saved 338 people. Both GDACS and USGS's PAGER system rate the event a Red alert for high humanitarian impact, with GDACS estimating about 5.2 million people within zones of MMI VII or greater shaking. The government has activated emergency coordination centres in Bogotá, Quibdó, Armenia and Cali, and the international response continues to scale up.

impact.summary: OCHA Colombia's Flash Update 007 and the Addendum to the Humanitarian Response Plan (data as of 17 August 2026) confirm 304 deaths, 4,400 injured and 426 missing, with 186,182 people (121,470 families) affected across 15 departments and 472 municipalities; 29,554 homes have been destroyed and 134,341 affected in total, with 267 residential buildings collapsed. Search and rescue operations have rescued 338 people. GDACS rates the event a Red alert (score 2.2) with about 5.2 million people in zones of MMI VII or greater shaking, and USGS's PAGER alert is also Red.

updates.text: OCHA Colombia's Flash Update 007 and the addendum to the Humanitarian Response Plan (data as of 17 August) raised the toll to 304 deaths, 4,400 injured and 426 missing, with 186,182 people (121,470 families) affected across 15 departments and 472 municipalities; homes destroyed rose to 29,554 and search-and-rescue operations had saved 338 people.

OCHA Colombia's Flash Update 006 (data as of 14 August, 18:30 local time) raised the toll to 287 deaths, 3,975 injured and 378 missing, with 135,179 people (56,448 families) affected across 15 departments and 437 municipalities, 13,077 homes destroyed, and 183 aftershocks recorded since the mainshock.

OCHA Colombia's Flash Update 005 (data as of 13 August, 18:30 local time) reported 266 deaths and 53,816 people (25,872 families) affected across 13 departments and 401 municipalities, with 11,789 homes destroyed, warning that figures may increase due to access constraints and possible underreporting.
USGS's PAGER alert for the earthquake was raised from Orange to Red as of 06:30 UTC on 13 August.

OCHA Colombia's Flash Update 004 (data as of 12 August, 18:30 local time) reported at least 241 fatalities, 3,771 injured and 49,214 people affected (30,324 families) across 13 departments, with damage to more than 54,900 homes; a USD 5 million CERF allocation was announced to scale up the emergency response.

GDACS escalated the event to a Red alert for high humanitarian impact, raising its score from 1.7 to 2.2 and its estimate of people within zones of MMI VII or greater shaking from about 1.5 million to about 5.2 million.

UN News, citing Colombia's president, reported more than 180 dead and hundreds injured, with nearly 5,000 homes damaged and 387 destroyed, 61 buildings collapsed, and more than 550 educational institutions, 24 health facilities and more than 350 community centres affected; the government activated emergency coordination centres in Bogotá, Quibdó, Armenia and Cali and requested UN support.

Servicio Geológico Colombiano confirmed the magnitude 7.4 event at a depth of about 103 km, recorded 18 aftershocks by midday, and described it as the seismic event of greatest magnitude recorded in Colombia in the 21st century, with more than 12,000 people from 900 populated centres reporting having felt it.
